chapter: Scrapbook: family, baseball and musician friends
title: Second Line profile and semi-pro baseball
summary: A 1953 Second Line profile prompts Riddick to describe seven years of semi-pro baseball until his eyesight failed.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. This is the Second Line magazine. Yeah. May 1953. Meet Jaffer.
It has an article in it by Dick Allen.
Mm-hmm. On the next page, I think.
Yeah. You see, Halfway House is in that. Bill Whitmore. Yeah. I used to date his niece, as a matter of fact.
Now, this was written by Doc Suchon.
Mm-hmm. We'll look that up. We got a copy of that. We got a... We got a... Insect in here. We got him now.
See, his hobbies are hunting and fishing and woodworking and landscape and gardening.
Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Seven years in semi-pro ball?

Oh, yes. What did you play? What... Every position on the field. I caught, I pitched. Mm-hmm. First base, second base, shortstop, anything in the world. Mm-hmm. They call that a general utilities, man.

So, my eyes began to fool me and I began to get hit. I had to quit. Yeah. My nose has been broken from being hit right in the face with a baseball because I misjudged. And the doctor told me that even one of these days you're going to get your brains knocked out, he says, your eyes are not far anymore.
Who was that pitcher? Ron Durant or something like that? They say he wore bottle caps for glasses. And all the batters were afraid of him for some reason.
